title: A website or business app your team can use.
content:
If your website hides your services, forms lose inquiries, or staff copy information between tools, start with the workflow. We build marketing websites, portals, and business applications around the tasks your customers and team need to complete.
Deliverables:
A written scope, page or workflow map, and integration requirements
Responsive implementation, agreed CMS or application features, and inquiry paths
Testing of core workflows, launch checklist, and handoff documentation
Scope:
A brochure website package does not include an unlimited custom application. Authentication, complex data migration, external APIs, hosting, software licenses, and ongoing operations are scoped separately. You provide access, approved content, and feedback; we agree on acceptance checks before development.
Pricing basis:
Published Web packages provide a starting point for websites. Application pricing depends on roles, workflows, data, integrations, and testing requirements. Confirm what is included in a written proposal.
Can you build a business application instead of a marketing site? Yes. We first define users, permissions, data, workflows, and integrations, then quote the application scope separately from a website package.
Can we keep our existing CMS? We review its access, templates, data, and integration limits before recommending an extension or migration.
How long will development take? The schedule depends on the approved scope, content readiness, integrations, and review cycles. Milestones are agreed after discovery.
Will the site generate leads automatically? We can implement clear inquiry paths and measurement. Traffic, visitor fit, and commercial results require ongoing review; no lead volume is guaranteed.
Do you work outside Long Island? KDH is based in Freeport, serves Long Island and NYC, and can deliver projects remotely.

title: Make your offer easier to understand.
content:
When customers cannot find the right service or know what to do next, a redesign needs more than a new visual style. We clarify page structure, content hierarchy, mobile navigation, and inquiry paths for your audience.
Deliverables:
Discovery notes, page inventory, and a proposed information structure
Wireframes and responsive page designs for agreed templates
Design review, implementation handoff, and agreed accessibility and mobile checks
Scope:
We agree on pages, templates, revisions, and whether development is included. Photography, brand identity creation, ongoing copywriting, and extensive content migration require their own scope. You approve factual claims and supply assets you have permission to use.
Pricing basis:
Web package totals below cover the published package scope. A design-only engagement or larger redesign is quoted by templates, content needs, implementation work, and review rounds.
Can you redesign without replacing everything? We review the existing structure and identify the pages, navigation, and interactions that need attention.
Is development included? The proposal states whether the work includes implementation, a design handoff, or both.
Can you help organize our content? Yes. We can map key messages and page structure. Content production and migration volumes are agreed separately.
Will the design work on phones? Responsive layouts and checks of agreed mobile journeys form part of the design scope.
Does a redesign guarantee more inquiries? No. We can improve clarity and make inquiry paths measurable, then evaluate results with real visitors.
David Dare MD portfolio: Treatment information hierarchy and appointment pathways; contribution details are described in the portfolio. https://kingdomdesignhouse.com/case-studies/daremd/

title: Connect useful content to a measurable next step.
content:
Traffic alone does not explain whether people can find your services or become customers. We review technical search foundations, service content, internal links, and inquiry measurement so you can see where the funnel needs work.
Deliverables:
A technical and content audit with prioritized actions
Agreed improvements to metadata, indexing, internal links, and service content
Consent-aware conversion measurement and a reporting framework tied to inquiries
Scope:
Search rankings, inclusion in AI answers, and inquiry volumes are not guaranteed. Media spend, paid campaign management, large content programs, and social publishing require an explicit scope. Account access and historical Search Console and GA4 data are dependencies.
Pricing basis:
SEO setup is part of the relevant published Web package scope. Ongoing marketing work depends on the audit, pages, content production, and reporting cadence; a support price is not an unlimited marketing retainer.
Do you guarantee a first-page ranking? No. Search platforms decide what to index and show. We focus on useful content and technical foundations that can be reviewed.
How do you measure success? Review search impressions and clicks, then confirmed inquiries, qualified conversations, consultations, proposals, and revenue. Keep engagement separate from leads.
Can you optimize for AI search? We apply conventional SEO: accessible text, internal links, accurate metadata, and structured data that matches visible content. Inclusion in AI answers is not guaranteed.
Do I need paid ads? Not necessarily. We first assess whether organic demand and the existing website support your goals. Paid campaigns are a separate decision and scope.
When should we review progress? Review the funnel weekly and compare 28-day search periods. Evaluate inquiry quality and commercial outcomes after 60–90 days before expanding content.
Assistant comparison guide: Useful buyer education connected to a relevant service and inquiry path. https://kingdomdesignhouse.com/guides/custom-ai-assistant-vs-chatbot/

title: Keep your website useful after launch.
content:
Broken forms, outdated content, plugin changes, and slow pages can interrupt the customer journey. We start with an audit and agree on routine maintenance, update priorities, and a process for reporting issues.
Deliverables:
An agreed maintenance scope and access inventory
Scheduled updates, content changes, or performance work within the selected plan
Checks of key inquiry paths, reporting, and handoff notes for changes
Scope:
Response times, service hours, backups, and monitoring must be agreed in writing. Support does not promise uninterrupted uptime or unlimited development. Emergency recovery, major redesigns, hosting, licenses, and new integrations may require separate work.
Pricing basis:
Published Web support prices are $150, $250, and $500 per month for the corresponding package scope. Existing websites are assessed before recommending a plan. Setup totals below apply to website projects, not automatically to support-only work.
Can you support a site you did not build? We review its framework, hosting, dependencies, access, and existing issues before confirming scope.
Are content edits included? The plan defines the kinds and volume of edits included. Larger content changes and new features are estimated separately.
Is support available 24/7? Service hours, response targets, and any emergency arrangements must be explicitly agreed.
Will you check our contact form? Key inquiry paths can be included in the maintenance checklist with safe test procedures and delivery checks.
Can we add features later? Yes. We assess new features separately and agree on cost, schedule, and acceptance checks.
DermCare Management portfolio: Modular content and responsive templates illustrate a maintainable structure; no ongoing support contract or uptime result is asserted. https://kingdomdesignhouse.com/case-studies/dermcare/

title: Start with a business task, then choose the AI.
content:
When staff repeatedly answer the same questions or transfer information between tools, an assistant may help. We scope the knowledge sources, actions, permissions, handoff, and failure cases before building a prototype.
Deliverables:
A workflow map, approved knowledge sources, and success and failure criteria
A prototype assistant or integration with scoped permissions and a human fallback
Evaluation examples, integration checks, deployment notes, and an update process
Scope:
AI responses can be incomplete or incorrect. Human review is required for consequential decisions. Model usage, hosting, vector storage, external licenses, data cleanup, and ongoing evaluation are scoped separately. Do not use the public demo for sensitive records or patient information.
Pricing basis:
Published AI setup totals start at $4,000 with support from $300 per month. The final scope depends on retrieval sources, integrations, actions, evaluation, and operating requirements. Third-party usage charges are separate and vary with traffic and configuration.
How is a custom assistant different from a basic chatbot? A fixed flow suits predictable questions. A custom assistant can retrieve approved knowledge and connect to tools, but needs more evaluation, maintenance, and oversight.
Can it connect to our CRM? We scope supported APIs, field mapping, permissions, retries, and failure handling. Jarvis has an implemented HubSpot handoff; your integration requires its own scope and verification.
Will it always answer correctly? No. We test representative questions, provide a human fallback, and define tasks the assistant must not perform.
What costs continue after launch? Support, model usage, hosting, retrieval storage, integration subscriptions, and content updates may continue. We identify these in the proposal rather than promise a fixed usage bill.
Can I try an example? Use the Jarvis demo for business questions and avoid sensitive information. It is a working assistant and may create a follow-up inquiry if you provide project and contact details.
Jarvis lead assistant: A working KDH assistant with retrieval, structured inquiry extraction, Contact fallback, and a HubSpot handoff implemented in this repository. https://kingdomdesignhouse.com/ai-group/solutions/ai-lead-assistant/

title: AI Lead Assistant & Jarvis Demo | Long Island & NYC
content:
Jarvis is the working assistant on this website. It answers questions using approved knowledge and retrieved site content, gathers business project details during a conversation, and can pass a follow-up inquiry to HubSpot. Open the demo to ask about a service, scope, or pricing. Providing contact and project details may create a real inquiry; do not use it for test submissions or sensitive information.
What the demo can demonstrate
Ask about KDH’s Web and AI services, compare package setup and support prices, or describe a business workflow. Jarvis uses the site’s retrieval service for grounded answers and extracts structured contact and project information for follow-up. It can still misunderstand a question or use outdated retrieved information.
Homepage, floating, and service-page buttons open the same conversation for the browser tab session. Service starters are editable drafts; they do not send a message automatically.
Qualification and human handoff
Useful qualification includes the requested service, project description, business, budget, and timeline when the visitor chooses to provide them. The server requires an email plus a service, description, or another inquiry indicator before attempting CRM synchronization.
The implemented HubSpot workflow upserts the contact and attempts related deal and follow-up ticket synchronization when enough project detail is available. Contact acceptance confirms receipt; a deal or ticket can still fail separately. The assistant offers a Contact form fallback, and a person must review the inquiry and follow up. It does not book a consultation or promise a response automatically.
Design for failure and ongoing care
Test irrelevant questions, missing data, ambiguous service requests, API failures, and failed handoffs. Keep actions restricted, review answers against approved content, and give visitors a way to reach a person.
Knowledge sources need refreshing when services, prices, or contributions change. Model and retrieval usage, hosting, integration subscriptions, and evaluation are operating costs in addition to the published setup and support scope.
What this example does not prove
This working example does not establish a measured increase in leads, sales, or revenue. Evaluate a proposed assistant against your own workflow and measurement baseline.
The public demo is for business inquiries. It is not a patient intake system, an emergency channel, or an autonomous decision-maker. Avoid patient data, credentials, and confidential records.
Does opening the demo create a lead? No. Opening a chat is engagement. An inquiry is confirmed only after the server reports successful CRM acceptance.
Can the handoff fail? Yes. CRM contact, deal, or ticket operations can fail. A Contact fallback stays available, and failed CRM acceptance is not counted as a lead.
Does the assistant replace a person? No. It can help with discovery and collecting information. People review requests, confirm scope, and handle decisions and follow-up.
What does an assistant cost? Published AI setup totals are $4,000, $6,000, and $8,000, with corresponding support at $300, $500, and $800 per month. Integrations and operating usage depend on the agreed scope.
Can I try it without sharing contact details? Yes. Ask a business or service question. Contact details are needed only if you want a follow-up inquiry.
Custom assistant vs chatbot: Compare simpler fixed flows with retrieval and integration requirements before choosing a build.

title: Custom AI Assistant vs Chatbot: Fit, Costs & Maintenance
content:
The labels overlap: many products called chatbots already use generative AI. A more useful comparison is a fixed flow or FAQ tool versus an assistant that retrieves business knowledge and can connect to other systems. Choose based on the task, information, operating cost, and review your team can support.
When a simpler flow is enough
A short FAQ, service selector, or structured inquiry form can be easier to operate than an open-ended assistant. If every visitor needs the same few choices, define those choices clearly and provide a person to contact when the flow does not fit.
When retrieval and integration add value
A custom assistant may be useful when visitors ask varied questions across approved information or staff need a specific workflow spanning tools. Start with a narrow task and representative test questions. An assistant still needs accurate sources and explicit rules for what it may do.
Compare the full cost of operation
Compare implementation effort, subscription and usage charges, hosting, storage, integration licenses, support, and the time people spend maintaining and reviewing the system. Avoid choosing based only on the demo or setup price.
KDH publishes AI setup totals from $4,000 and support from $300 per month. These are package starting points, not a guaranteed total operating bill. A simpler existing tool may be more appropriate for a small, fixed task.
Decide how a person takes over
Define a clear handoff for uncertainty, missing information, and integration failure. Keep consequential decisions with people, restrict actions, and avoid collecting sensitive records in a public business demo.
Jarvis demonstrates service questions and an implemented HubSpot inquiry handoff. Opening it is engagement; successful CRM acceptance or Contact notification delivery is the point at which KDH records an inquiry.
Is an AI assistant always better? No. A fixed flow or ordinary form may solve the problem with less cost and maintenance.
Can an assistant make mistakes with approved sources? Yes. Retrieval can miss context and generated answers can be incorrect. Use evaluation questions, clear limitations, and human escalation.
What should I prepare before choosing? List common questions, approved sources, systems involved, expected usage, who maintains the content, and the decisions a person must review.
Will either option increase sales? Neither guarantees sales. Measure confirmed inquiries and qualified commercial outcomes against a real baseline.
Explore Jarvis: Try a service conversation before deciding whether a similar assistant fits your workflow.
